label: Neutral substitution rate equals the mutation rate
statement_en: For neutral mutations the long-run rate of molecular substitution equals the mutation rate per generation, independent of population size, which yields a molecular clock.

scope.basis: a theorem about a model: it applies wherever the design supplies the quantities it uses and accepts the hypotheses in scope.assumed
kernelChecked: A neutral absorbing chain on {0..M} copies (stochastic, mean-preserving, both ends absorbing, positive one-step escape from every interior state) fixes a mutant with probability i/M, with an explicit geometric error bound at every finite time t.
The Wright-Fisher binomial kernel is such a chain (row sums, mean preservation and absorption proved from Bernstein polynomial identities).
With u = 1/M the defined substitution rate M * mu * u equals mu, also in the diploid 2N form and as the t -> infinity limit.
assumed: Constant population size and Wright-Fisher reproduction (non-overlapping generations, multinomial sampling).

Independent fates of mutants: the substitution rate is DEFINED, as in Kimura 1968, as (new mutants per generation) x (fixation probability of one mutant). Interference between lineages is excluded by that definition, not proved absent.
The mutation rate mu per copy per generation is a free parameter; nothing here measures it.

sources: Evolutionary Rate at the Molecular Level (1968)

non_vacuity_witness.statement: the Wright-Fisher binomial chain is a NeutralChain for every M > 0 (an instance, defined in the module)
